title: Nivat's conjecture
abstract: For every configuration on the integer plane over an arbitrary finite alphabet, a positive k by n rectangle with at most k*n occurring translated patterns forces a nonzero global period of the original configuration. The statement includes equality at the complexity threshold and rectangles of width or height one. The Lean proof is due to Catenation, my custom agentic framework, translating the argument in my paper into Lean. The proof uses Laurent annihilators, a sharp periodic-wedge complexity bound, generating polygons, and selection of the same nonperiodic orbit point throughout the periodic-background construction. Its mathematical setting is multidimensional symbolic dynamics and combinatorics of low-complexity configurations. The independent Challenge states the full conjecture using only standard Mathlib notions.
